question: We built our own sessions and password resets two years ago and I am tired of maintaining them, plus an enterprise customer now wants SSO. Node backend, React front end, a few thousand users to migrate. Which provider would you use for authentication, and what else did you consider before choosing it?
summary: Test a migrated login and the first enterprise SSO connection. The recorded mentions do not show whether an agent can complete these tasks.

items.title: Test the documented integration
items.finding: The migration API and SSO guides provide an integration route. The scan missed an agent entry file and account signup link, and did not establish project-key creation. Those observations do not tell us whether migrated users can sign in. Provide an authorized test project before evaluating that task.
items.nextStep: Import synthetic legacy members with an agreed supported password-hash format and preserved external IDs; verify valid and rejected sign-ins. Configure one test organization and identity provider, complete enterprise SSO from React, and verify the Node session and organization mapping.
items.validation: Record import results, identity mapping, accepted and rejected logins, session checks and account handoffs. Use only verified synthetic identities for the migration endpoint.

sources.note: Migration options, password compatibility, external IDs and organization mapping.
B2B password migration API; requires previously verified email ownership.
React SSO initiation and callback completion.

items.title: Make the relevant entry cost easy to check
items.finding: The pricing description contains no amount or entry condition. That metadata observation does not explain recommendation frequency.
items.nextStep: Check the current plan for this task before adding a concrete entry condition to the description. Keep paid features and hosted versus local costs distinct.
items.validation: Any proposed wording must match the chosen plan. No recommendation uplift has been measured.

sources.note: Pricing page whose description was captured in the scan.
